title: Maximum Product of First and Last Elements of a Subsequence
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer m, find the maximum product of the first and last elements in any subsequence of nums that has exactly m elements.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer m, find the maximum product of the first and last elements in any subsequence of nums that has exactly m elements.
constraints: nums has up to 100,000 integers and 1 <= m <= len(nums).
Choose exactly m indices in increasing order.
Maximize the product of values at the first and last chosen indices; for m=1 this is the selected value squared.
hints: For a last index j, any first index at most j-m+1 can be completed to an m-element subsequence.
Maintain the minimum and maximum eligible first values; one of them maximizes its product with the current last value.
As j advances, add nums[j-m+1] to prefix extrema and test nums[j] times both extrema.
All intermediate indices can be chosen arbitrarily, so endpoint spacing is the only feasibility condition; extrema handle both positive and negative products.
editorial: All intermediate indices can be chosen arbitrarily, so endpoint spacing is the only feasibility condition; extrema handle both positive and negative products.

tests.explanation: Choosing the singleton negative nine uses it as both endpoints, producing 81.
A subsequence beginning at negative five and ending at negative four produces 20.
